findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 140 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 4/mm3. Protein 54 mg/dL (mildly elevated). Glucose 62 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.70). Gram stain: no organisms. Culture: no growth to date. Cytology: no malignant cells. Mildly elevated protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation). Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description: Degenerative disc bulges and uncovertebral hypertrophy with moderate canal narrowing; CSF preserved around the cord; mild left C6-C7 foraminal narrowing.
Normal calibre and signal. No compression. No intramedullary enhancement.
Smooth enhancement of the cauda equina nerve roots after gadolinium.

output.impression: 1. Moderate degenerative canal narrowing at C5-C6 and C6-C7 without cord compression or cord signal change. 2. Smooth enhancement of the cauda equina nerve roots. 3. No intramedullary lesion.
Bedside respiratory function on hospital day 2: FVC 2.3 L (88% predicted; 34 mL/kg at 68 kg). MIP -46 cmH2O. MEP 72 cmH2O. Cough effective.

findings: Atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate 64-96 bpm
output.impression: 24-hour continuous telemetry. Atrial fibrillation throughout with ventricular rate 64-96 bpm. No pauses over 2 seconds and no ventricular arrhythmia. Blood pressure 124/72 to 158/90 mmHg.
output.rhythm_summary: Atrial fibrillation throughout with controlled rate. No pauses.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week; here motor and sensory demyelination in several nerves, separate from the chronic right peroneal neuropathy
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and separate a polyradiculoneuropathy from a cervical radiculopathy, a ganglionopathy and the chronic peroneal neuropathy [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infectious and malignant causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No acute infarct on diffusion imaging; chronic small vessel change only
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI with diffusion to complete the stroke work-up of the wake-up asymmetric deficit
action_criteria.rationale: A wake-up, initially asymmetric sensory deficit in a patient with atrial fibrillation was triaged as stroke; CT and CTA cannot exclude a small cardioembolic infarct.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Degenerative cervical canal narrowing without cord compression or cord signal change; nerve root enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Contrast spine MRI for known cervical canal stenosis with asymmetric hand symptoms
action_criteria.rationale: New left hand numbness and grip weakness in a patient with known cervical canal stenosis raise cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy, and marked asymmetry makes GBS less likely [EAN_PNS_2023]; the MRI settles it.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics (potassium, glucose, CK) and give the baseline before IVIg; liver tests and albumin carry prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Weakness is still spreading on day 2; serial FVC, MIP and MEP detect respiratory involvement before it is clinically evident [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: rate-controlled atrial fibrillation 64-96 bpm without pauses and blood pressure 124/72 to 158/90 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS; on propranolol with atrial fibrillation, bradyarrhythmia and hypotension need continuous monitoring while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Rate-controlled atrial fibrillation (82 bpm) with QRS 88 ms and QTc 442 ms: baseline rhythm and QTc on citalopram and solifenacin
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline ECG gives the rhythm and the QTc on two QT-relevant drugs and screens for autonomic dysrhythmia [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Propranolol adds to autonomic bradycardia and hypotension; solifenacin can worsen urinary retention and prolongs QT with citalopram; no anticoagulant, so no bleeding interaction with the LP
action_criteria.label: Check the medication list for interactions with propranolol, solifenacin, citalopram, amlodipine and atorvastatin before IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: Her beta-blocker and antimuscarinic interact with the autonomic involvement of GBS and change monitoring and dosing; confirming that no anticoagulant is taken clears the lumbar puncture.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not withhold immunotherapy because sensory symptoms predominate: she cannot walk unaided and is progressing.
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to a monitored bed with FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours while weakness spreads; move to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 60% predicted or 20 mL/kg (about 1.4 L at 68 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -40 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, FVC falls by more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough develops [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 27 g/day at 68 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because she cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3) and is still progressing, despite the sensory predominance; plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses; reduce or hold propranolol if bradycardia or hypotension develops.
Measure post-void residual volumes and stop solifenacin if urinary retention develops (antimuscarinic on top of possible autonomic bladder involvement).

Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while she cannot walk [Leonhard_2019]; plan oral anticoagulation for the atrial fibrillation (age 75, hypertension) after the lumbar puncture.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography belongs to the outpatient work-up of the new atrial fibrillation; it does not contribute to the neurological diagnosis, and no infarct was found.
CT and CT angiography were done at presentation; a repeat head CT adds nothing, and CT does not show nerve roots.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, early AIDP with sensory-predominant presentation

differential.key_features: Known canal stenosis and asymmetric left hand symptoms raise it, but reflexes are depressed with flexor plantars and no Hoffmann sign, both feet are involved, the NCS shows demyelination in several nerves, and the MRI shows no cord compression or signal change.
Wake-up onset with atrial fibrillation, but bilateral feet and hands are involved, reflexes are lost, and diffusion MRI shows no infarct.
Sensory ataxia and prior colon cancer raise it, but motor conduction slowing, absent F-waves and distal weakness place the lesion in the roots and nerves, not the dorsal root ganglia.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
Vitamin B12 384 pg/mL and folate normal; areflexia and demyelinating NCS over two days do not fit.

key_clinical_evidence: Distal sensory symptoms and weakness spreading over 24 hours, reflexes lost by day 2, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 54 mg/dL, 4 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating sensorimotor NCS: GBS with sensory predominance after a respiratory illness.
Reflexes may be normal in the first days of GBS; a normal first examination does not exclude it [EAN_PNS_2023].
Marked asymmetry and a known cervical stenosis call for spine imaging before the deficit is attributed to GBS; here the MRI shows no cord compression [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].
Motor conduction slowing and absent F-waves separate a polyradiculoneuropathy from a sensory ganglionopathy, which spares motor conduction.
Inability to walk unaided within 2 weeks of onset is the indication for IVIg or plasma exchange, whatever the sensory predominance [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Depressed reflexes with flexor plantars, bilateral foot and hand involvement, new demyelination in several nerves on top of the unchanged right peroneal lesion, and an MRI without cord compression point to an acute polyradiculoneuropathy.
red_herrings.data_point: Known cervical canal stenosis and chronic right foot drop
red_herrings.intended_effect: Invites attributing the left hand symptoms to cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy and the foot weakness to the old peroneal neuropathy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Bilateral symptoms that spread over 24 hours, loss of reflexes on day 2 and a normal diffusion MRI exclude stroke.
red_herrings.data_point: Wake-up onset of an asymmetric sensory deficit in a patient with atrial fibrillation
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors on cardioembolic stroke; the stroke pathway was activated at presentation.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Reflexes can be preserved in the first days of GBS; they were depressed or absent by day 2.
red_herrings.data_point: Normal 2+ reflexes on the admission examination
red_herrings.intended_effect: Normal reflexes seem to argue against GBS.

sequence_constraints.reason: Potassium and renal function are needed to judge the QT interactions and the IVIg dose.

interactions: Propranolol: beta-blockade adds to bradycardia and hypotension from autonomic dysfunction and blunts compensatory tachycardia (monitor heart rate and blood pressure; relative caution).
Solifenacin: antimuscarinic; can cause or worsen urinary retention and constipation, and carries a QT-prolongation warning (monitor bladder emptying).
Citalopram: dose-dependent QT prolongation (maximum 20 mg/day over age 60); additive with other QT-prolonging drugs and with hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia.
Amlodipine: additive hypotension with the fluid shifts of plasma exchange (relative caution).
Atorvastatin: no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange.
No oral anticoagulant or antiplatelet on the list; no bleeding interaction with lumbar puncture or central venous access.
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange with the current medication list
general.summary: Category-level review of citalopram, solifenacin, amlodipine, atorvastatin and propranolol against IVIg and plasma exchange.
warnings: IVIg carries a dose-related thrombotic risk; age, atrial fibrillation and immobility add to it.

findings: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate
ecg.interpretation: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate (82 bpm). QRS 88 ms. QTc 442 ms (normal). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: CRP 7.2 mg/L (elevated). ESR 32 mm/hr (elevated). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

additional_observations: No cortical or brainstem lesion. No abnormal enhancement after gadolinium. No microhaemorrhages.

findings.location: Bilateral periventricular and subcortical white matter

mri.impression: 1. No acute infarct on diffusion-weighted imaging. 2. Scattered subcortical and periventricular white matter FLAIR hyperintensities, consistent with chronic small vessel ischaemic change. 3. No brainstem lesion and no abnormal enhancement.

findings.finding: DML 7.6 ms (prolonged); CV 32 m/s (reduced); CMAP 4.4 mV
DML 7.8 ms (prolonged); CV 30 m/s (reduced); CMAP 1.9 mV (reduced)
CMAP 0.8 mV (reduced) with conduction slowing across the fibular head, as on the 2019 study
Absent bilateral median; absent bilateral peroneal

Left tibialis anterior and left first dorsal interosseous: reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units, no fibrillation potentials; right tibialis anterior: large chronic reinnervated units, no fibrillation potentials

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials (present in 2019); reduced median and left ulnar sensory amplitudes with sensory slowing. 2. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in the median and left peroneal motor nerves. 3. Absent F-waves (median and peroneal) and absent H-reflexes. 4. Chronic right peroneal neuropathy at the fibular head, unchanged from 2019. 5. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Pattern consistent with an acquired demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy, superimposed on a chronic right peroneal neuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.comparison: 2019 study: right peroneal neuropathy at the fibular head, sural SNAPs present

metadata.difficulty_description: Wake-up sensory-predominant GBS triaged as stroke in a patient with atrial fibrillation, cervical stenosis and a chronic foot drop; reflexes normal on day 1 and depressed by day 2.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required and 3 recommended actions, 3 red herrings; background diagnoses that each explain part of the picture and an evolving examination.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Wake-up onset left hand and bilateral foot paresthesias and weakness, initially triaged as stroke, with prior viral illness 2 weeks ago.

past_medical_history: Colon adenocarcinoma resected in 2015, no recurrence on surveillance
Longstanding right foot drop (right peroneal neuropathy at the fibular head on a nerve conduction study in 2019)
Atrial fibrillation (recent diagnosis, under investigation; not anticoagulated)

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. E. is a 75-year-old woman with a history of colon adenocarcinoma resected in 2015 without recurrence, cervical canal stenosis, a longstanding right foot drop and recently diagnosed atrial fibrillation who was brought to the emergency department yesterday after waking with numbness of the left hand and tingling of both feet. She was assessed as a possible stroke; thrombolysis was not given because the time of onset was unknown, and CT and CT angiography of the head and neck showed no haemorrhage and no large-vessel occlusion. On that admission examination she had decreased sensation in the left hand and both forefeet in a non-dermatomal distribution, normal (2+) reflexes and relatively preserved strength, yet she could not walk without help. She was admitted for brain MRI. Over the following 24 hours the numbness spread and she became weaker in both feet and both hands. Two weeks before presentation she had 2-3 days of cough, fever and myalgias that resolved without treatment. She has no back or neck pain, no bladder or bowel change, no double vision and no difficulty swallowing or breathing. The examination below is from the second hospital day.

neurological_exam.additional: Romberg sign positive. Unable to stand without support with eyes closed.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact finger-nose. Mildly impaired heel-shin bilaterally.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness. No ptosis. No diplopia.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to walk independently; requires the assistance of one person.
neurological_exam.motor: Upper limbs: grip 4/5 left, 4+/5 right; finger abduction 4/5 left, 4+/5 right; proximal strength 5/5. Lower limbs: ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 left, 3+/5 right (chronic right foot drop, 4/5 at baseline), toe extension 3/5 bilaterally; hip flexion and knee extension 5/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps, triceps and brachioradialis 1+ bilaterally, knee 1+ bilaterally, ankle absent bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced pinprick and light touch in the left hand to the wrist in a non-dermatomal distribution; tingling of the right fingertips without objective loss; reduced pinprick over both forefeet; vibration reduced to the ankles bilaterally. No sensory level.
